phrases.translation: The command of Allah is at hand, so do not hasten it. Glorified and Exalted is He above what they associate ˹with Him in worship˺
phrases.explanation: The verse answers people who demand that the promised judgment come immediately: Allah’s decree will arrive at its appointed time, so humans should not presume to set its timing. It closes by declaring Allah exalted above every partner attributed to Him.

phrases.translation: He sends down the angels with revelation by His command to whoever He wills of His servants, ˹stating:˺ “Warn ˹humanity˺ that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Me, so be mindful of Me ˹alone˺.”
phrases.explanation: Revelation comes through angels by Allah’s command to chosen servants, who are charged to warn humanity that none deserves worship but Him. The warning joins monotheism with mindfulness, asking people to live in awareness of their Creator.

phrases.translation: He created the heavens and the earth for a purpose. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him ˹in worship˺
phrases.explanation: The heavens and earth are created with purpose, not as an accident or a meaningless realm. Their order points to divine wisdom, and Allah is exalted above the partners people associate with Him.

phrases.translation: He created humans from a sperm-drop, then—behold!—they openly challenge ˹Him˺
phrases.explanation: Human beings begin from a small drop, yet some grow into open opponents of their Creator. The contrast challenges human arrogance by recalling how dependent and modest our origin is.

phrases.translation: And He created the cattle for you as a source of warmth, food, and ˹many other˺ benefits
phrases.explanation: Cattle provide warmth, food, and many other benefits. The verse presents familiar livelihoods as gifts from Allah, inviting people to notice the care and practical provision embedded in everyday life.

phrases.translation: They are also pleasing to you when you bring them home and when you take them out to graze
phrases.explanation: The cattle bring pleasure both when they return home and when they are taken out to graze. Their value is not only material. Their presence and daily rhythms are also a source of beauty and enjoyment.

phrases.translation: And they carry your loads to ˹distant˺ lands which you could not otherwise reach without great hardship. Surely your Lord is Ever Gracious, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Cattle carry heavy loads to distant places that people could otherwise reach only with great hardship. The verse recognizes the practical support animals provide and concludes by describing the Lord as gracious and merciful.

phrases.translation: ˹He also created˺ horses, mules, and donkeys for your transportation and adornment. And He creates what you do not know
phrases.explanation: Horses, mules, and donkeys serve for transport and adornment, reflecting both usefulness and beauty. The closing words widen the perspective beyond known animals: Allah continues to create things people do not yet know.

phrases.translation: It is upon Allah ˹alone˺ to ˹clearly˺ show the Straight Way. Other ways are deviant. Had He willed, He would have easily imposed guidance upon all of you
phrases.explanation: Allah makes the Straight Way clear, while other routes lead away from it. The verse also says that Allah could have compelled universal guidance, showing that the existence of varied human choices is not beyond His power.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who sends down rain from the sky, from which you drink and by which plants grow for your cattle to graze
phrases.explanation: Rain is sent from the sky as water for people to drink and as a means for vegetation to grow for grazing animals. The same rain sustains human life and the livestock on which communities depend.

phrases.translation: With it He produces for you ˹various˺ crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and every type of fruit. Surely in this is a sign for those who reflect
phrases.explanation: Rain produces crops, olives, dates, grapes, and many other fruits. The variety of food arising from water and soil is offered as a sign for people who reflect on how provision reaches them.

phrases.translation: And He has subjected for your benefit the day and the night, the sun and the moon. And the stars have been subjected by His command. Surely in this are signs for those who understand
phrases.explanation: Day and night, the sun and moon, and the stars all operate under Allah’s command for human benefit. Their dependable patterns help life and navigation, and invite thoughtful recognition of the order behind them.

phrases.translation: And ˹He subjected˺ for you whatever He has created on earth of varying colours. Surely in this is a sign for those who are mindful
phrases.explanation: The earth contains created things of many colors and kinds. Their diversity is described as a sign for people mindful of Allah, encouraging attention to the richness of the world rather than treating it as ordinary or self-created.

phrases.translation: And He is the One Who has subjected the sea, so from it you may eat tender seafood and extract ornaments to wear. And you see the ships ploughing their way through it, so you may seek His bounty and give thanks ˹to Him˺
phrases.explanation: The sea provides seafood and materials for ornaments, while ships cross it so people can seek their livelihood. These benefits are connected to gratitude: travel and commerce are human efforts made possible within a world Allah has subjected for use.

phrases.translation: He has placed into the earth firm mountains, so it does not shake with you, as well as rivers, and pathways so you may find your way
phrases.explanation: Mountains, rivers, and pathways are described as features that help make the earth habitable and navigable. The verse draws attention to stability and orientation, two conditions people often rely on without noticing.

phrases.translation: Also by landmarks and stars do people find their way
phrases.explanation: Landmarks and stars help people find their way. Both familiar features on the ground and distant lights in the sky serve as means of orientation, turning the created world into a guide for travelers.

phrases.translation: Can the One Who creates be equal to those who do not? Will you not then be mindful
phrases.explanation: The verse contrasts the Creator with beings that do not create, asking whether they can be equal. The rhetorical question exposes the weakness of worshipping idols or other dependent things instead of the One who brings life into existence.

phrases.translation: If you tried to count Allah’s blessings, you would never be able to number them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: If people tried to count Allah’s blessings, they could never encompass them all. The verse joins this abundance with Allah’s forgiveness and mercy, reminding people that gratitude and hope belong together.

phrases.translation: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you reveal
phrases.explanation: Allah knows what people conceal as well as what they reveal. No intention or public action is hidden from Him, so the verse grounds accountability in complete divine knowledge rather than human observation alone.

phrases.translation: But those ˹idols˺ they invoke besides Allah cannot create anything—they themselves are created
phrases.explanation: The idols invoked besides Allah cannot create anything. They are themselves created. The contrast exposes a basic inconsistency in worshipping dependent objects as though they possessed the power and authority of the Creator.

phrases.translation: They are dead, not alive—not even knowing when their followers will be resurrected
phrases.explanation: The idols are lifeless and do not even know when their worshippers will be raised. Their inability to act or know the future sharply contrasts with the living, all-knowing Creator they are wrongly asked to represent.

phrases.translation: Your God is ˹only˺ One God. As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are in denial, and they are too proud
phrases.explanation: The passage states that God is one, then links denial of the Hereafter with hearts that refuse the truth and pride that resists it. Belief in accountability is presented as a matter of both conviction and humility.

phrases.translation: Without a doubt, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. He certainly does not like those who are too proud
phrases.explanation: Allah knows both hidden and public matters and does not love those who act arrogantly. This knowledge means rejection cannot be concealed, while the warning identifies pride as a spiritual barrier rather than a sign of strength.

phrases.translation: And when it is said to them, “What has your Lord revealed?” They say, “Ancient fables!”
phrases.explanation: When asked what has been revealed, the opponents dismiss it as old fables. Their answer replaces consideration of the message with ridicule, illustrating how a person can reject revelation without engaging with its claims.

phrases.translation: Let them bear their burdens in full on the Day of Judgment as well as some of the burdens of those they mislead without knowledge. Evil indeed is what they will bear
phrases.explanation: Those who mislead others bear their own wrongdoing and a share of the consequences connected to those they misguide. This does not erase the followers’ responsibility. The verse condemns leading people astray without knowledge.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those before them had plotted, but Allah struck at the ˹very˺ foundation of their structure, so the roof collapsed on top of them, and the torment came upon them from where they did not expect
phrases.explanation: Earlier plotters built schemes they thought secure, but their structure collapsed from its foundations and punishment came unexpectedly. The image shows that elaborate plans cannot protect wrongdoing when Allah’s judgment arrives.

phrases.translation: Then on the Day of Judgment He will humiliate them and say, “Where are My ˹so-called˺ associate-gods for whose sake you used to oppose ˹the believers˺?” Those gifted with knowledge will say, “Surely disgrace and misery today are upon the disbelievers.”
phrases.explanation: On Judgment Day, the false gods are exposed as powerless, and the knowledgeable testify that disgrace belongs to the disbelievers. The scene reverses worldly confidence: those who mocked warning face an undeniable public reckoning.

phrases.translation: Those whose souls the angels seize while they wrong themselves will then offer ˹full˺ submission ˹and say falsely,˺ “We did not do any evil.” ˹The angels will say,˺ “No! Surely Allah fully knows what you used to do
phrases.explanation: Some people will claim innocence when angels take their souls, despite having wronged themselves. The angels answer that Allah knows their deeds fully, so a last-minute denial cannot undo a life of wrongdoing.

phrases.translation: So enter the gates of Hell, to stay there forever. Indeed, what an evil home for the arrogant!”
phrases.explanation: The arrogant are told to enter Hell and remain there, described as an evil home. The verse presents pride not as a harmless attitude but as part of a pattern whose consequence is lasting punishment.

phrases.translation: And ˹when˺ it is said to those mindful ˹of Allah˺, “What has your Lord revealed?” They say, “All the best!” For those who do good in this world, there is goodness. But far better is the ˹eternal˺ Home of the Hereafter. How excellent indeed is the home of the righteous
phrases.explanation: When asked what was revealed, the mindful answer that it is good. Their response contrasts with the mockers and leads to a promise of good in this life and an even better, lasting home for the righteous.

phrases.translation: the Gardens of Eternity which they will enter, under which rivers flow. In it they will have whatever they desire. This is how Allah rewards the righteous—
phrases.explanation: The promised home is described as gardens beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous receive what they desire. The verse stresses enduring reward and begins a thought completed by the next verse.

phrases.translation: those whose souls the angels take while they are virtuous, saying ˹to them˺, “Peace be upon you! Enter Paradise for what you used to do.”
phrases.explanation: The angels greet the virtuous with peace as they take their souls and welcome them into Paradise. Their good deeds are named as the reason for this reward, linking earthly conduct with the Hereafter.

phrases.translation: Are they only awaiting the coming of the angels or the command of your Lord ˹O Prophet˺? So were those before them. And Allah never wronged them, but it was they who wronged themselves
phrases.explanation: The opponents are warned that they may be waiting for angels or Allah’s command, as earlier peoples did. Allah did not wrong those communities. Their own choices brought the consequences upon them.

phrases.translation: Then the evil ˹consequences˺ of their deeds overtook them, and they were overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule
phrases.explanation: The consequences of earlier people’s deeds eventually overtook them, and the punishment they had mocked became real. The verse warns that ridicule does not make a serious warning disappear or become harmless.

phrases.translation: The polytheists argue, “Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have worshipped anything other than Him, nor prohibited anything without His command.” So did those before them. Is not the messengers’ duty only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly
phrases.explanation: The polytheists blame Allah’s will for their idolatry and invented prohibitions, but the same excuse was used by earlier peoples. The verse then clarifies that messengers are responsible for clearly delivering the message, not forcing acceptance.

phrases.translation: We surely sent a messenger to every community, saying, “Worship Allah and shun false gods.” But some of them were guided by Allah, while others were destined to stray. So travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers
phrases.explanation: Every community received a messenger calling people to worship Allah and reject false gods. The verse notes differing responses, then invites travel to observe the fate of those who denied the message.

phrases.translation: Even though you ˹O Prophet˺ are keen on their guidance, Allah certainly does not guide those He leaves to stray, and they will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: Even the Prophet’s earnest desire cannot compel people to accept guidance. The verse places ultimate guidance with Allah and warns that those left in error will find no helper to rescue them from its outcome.

phrases.translation: They swear by Allah their most solemn oaths that Allah will never raise the dead to life. Yes ˹He will˺! It is a true promise binding on Him, but most people do not know
phrases.explanation: Some swear solemnly that the dead will never be raised, but Allah affirms that resurrection is a true promise. Their confidence in denial does not change the promise, though many people fail to understand it.

phrases.translation: ˹He will do that˺ to make clear to them what they disagreed on, and for the disbelievers to know that they were liars
phrases.explanation: Resurrection will make clear the matters people disputed and expose the falsehood of those who denied it. The Hereafter is therefore not only a return to life but also a final clarification of contested truth.

phrases.translation: If We ever will something ˹to exist˺, all We say is: “Be!” And it is
phrases.explanation: When Allah wills something to exist, His command is enough for it to come into being. The image of “Be” and it is expresses divine power without suggesting that creation requires human-like effort or delay.

phrases.translation: As for those who emigrated in ˹the cause of˺ Allah after being persecuted, We will surely bless them with a good home in this world. But the reward of the Hereafter is far better, if only they knew
phrases.explanation: The verse honors those who leave their homes because of persecution for faith, promising them a good home in this world and a far greater reward in the Hereafter. It offers hope to believers forced to endure hardship.

phrases.translation: ˹It is˺ they who have patiently endured, and in their Lord they put their trust
phrases.explanation: The emigrants are described by two qualities: they endured patiently and placed their trust in their Lord. Their reliance on Allah accompanies action and perseverance rather than replacing either one.

phrases.translation: We did not send ˹messengers˺ before you ˹O Prophet˺ except mere men inspired by Us. If you ˹polytheists˺ do not know ˹this already˺, then ask those who have knowledge ˹of the Scriptures˺
phrases.explanation: Earlier messengers were human beings who received revelation, not angels. Those unfamiliar with this history are directed to ask people knowledgeable about earlier Scriptures, grounding the claim in a continuing prophetic tradition.

phrases.translation: ˹We sent them˺ with clear proofs and divine Books. And We have sent down to you ˹O Prophet˺ the Reminder, so that you may explain to people what has been revealed for them, and perhaps they will reflect
phrases.explanation: Messengers came with clear proofs and revealed books, and the Prophet receives the Reminder to explain what has been sent to people. The purpose is reflection, not merely recitation without understanding.

phrases.translation: Do those who devise evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them? Or that the torment will not come upon them in ways they cannot comprehend
phrases.explanation: People who scheme evil are asked whether they feel secure from the earth swallowing them or punishment arriving unexpectedly. The questions challenge a false sense of safety and remind wrongdoers that their plans do not control events.

phrases.translation: Or that He will not seize them while they go about ˹their day˺, for then they will have no escape
phrases.explanation: Punishment could seize people while they go about their ordinary lives, leaving them no way to escape. The verse warns that wrongdoing is not safe simply because danger has not yet appeared.

phrases.translation: Or that He will not destroy them gradually? But your Lord is truly Ever Gracious, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: The warning includes gradual punishment, while Allah is described as gracious and merciful. The respite and mercy should not be mistaken for approval, but they leave room for people to turn back before consequences arrive.

phrases.translation: Have they not considered how the shadows of everything Allah has created incline to the right and the left ˹as the sun moves˺, totally submitting to Allah in all humility
phrases.explanation: The changing shadows of created things move as the sun shifts, a visible sign of the order of creation. Their submission is expressed through the way they follow the pattern Allah has set, without pride or resistance.

phrases.translation: And to Allah ˹alone˺ bows down ˹in submission˺ whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of living creatures, as do the angels—who are not too proud ˹to do so˺
phrases.explanation: All living creatures in the heavens and earth, along with the angels, bow to Allah. The angels are specifically described as free of arrogance, presenting humility before the Creator as the fitting response of creation.

phrases.translation: They fear their Lord above them, and do whatever they are commanded
phrases.explanation: The angels fear their Lord and carry out what they are commanded. Their obedience is not reluctant rebellion but reverence, reinforcing that even powerful unseen beings remain servants of Allah.

phrases.translation: And Allah has said, “Do not take two gods. There is only One God. So be in awe of Me ˹alone˺.”
phrases.explanation: Allah forbids taking two gods and declares that He alone is God, deserving awe and worship. The verse states the central principle of divine oneness in direct, unambiguous terms for all people.

phrases.translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him ˹alone˺ is the everlasting devotion. Will you then fear any other than Allah
phrases.explanation: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah, and lasting devotion is due to Him alone. The verse then asks why people would fear or worship anyone besides the One who owns all things.

phrases.translation: Whatever blessings you have are from Allah. Then whenever hardship touches you, to Him ˹alone˺ you cry ˹for help˺
phrases.explanation: Every blessing people enjoy comes from Allah. When hardship arrives, they instinctively call on Him for help, revealing a dependence that the verse invites them to acknowledge in ease as well as distress.

phrases.translation: Then as soon as He removes the hardship from you, a group of you associates ˹others˺ with their Lord ˹in worship˺
phrases.explanation: Once Allah removes hardship, some people return to associating others with Him. The contrast exposes a selective response: they seek the One God in crisis but fail to remain grateful when relief comes.

phrases.translation: only returning Our favours with ingratitude. So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know
phrases.explanation: They repay divine favors with ingratitude and are told that they will soon know the outcome. The warning challenges people who enjoy provision while denying the One who gives it.

phrases.translation: And they ˹even˺ assign to those ˹idols˺—who know nothing—a share of what We have provided for them. By Allah! You will certainly be questioned about whatever ˹lies˺ you used to fabricate ˹against Allah˺
phrases.explanation: The idolaters allocate a share of their provision to idols that know nothing, then face an oath that they will be questioned about their fabrications against Allah. The verse exposes both misplaced devotion and invented claims.

phrases.translation: And they attribute ˹angels as˺ daughters to Allah—glory be to Him!—the opposite of what they desire for themselves
phrases.explanation: Some attribute daughters, understood here as angels, to Allah while preferring sons for themselves. The verse rejects this double standard and declares Allah exalted above the claims people invent about Him.

phrases.translation: Whenever one of them is given the good news of a baby girl, his face grows gloomy, as he suppresses his rage
phrases.explanation: The birth of a daughter makes one of these men gloomy and angry. The verse exposes the shame and suppressed rage behind a culture that devalued girls, preparing to condemn the choices that follow.

phrases.translation: He hides himself from the people because of the bad news he has received. Should he keep her in disgrace, or bury her ˹alive˺ in the ground? Evil indeed is their judgment
phrases.explanation: The man hides from others while considering whether to keep the girl in humiliation or bury her alive. The verse condemns both the dishonor imposed on daughters and the atrocity of infanticide as an evil judgment.

phrases.translation: To those who disbelieve in the Hereafter belong all evil qualities, whereas to Allah belong the finest attributes. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: The verse contrasts the blameworthy qualities of those who deny the Hereafter with the highest and finest attributes belonging to Allah. It closes by affirming that Allah is mighty and wise, never subject to human double standards.

phrases.translation: If Allah were to punish people ˹immediately˺ for their wrongdoing, He would not have left a single living being on earth. But He delays them for an appointed term. And when their time arrives, they cannot delay it for a moment, nor could they advance it
phrases.explanation: If every wrongdoer were punished immediately, no living creature would remain. Allah instead sets an appointed term, but when it arrives no one can move it earlier or later, joining mercy and respite with certain accountability.

phrases.translation: They attribute to Allah what they hate ˹for themselves˺, and their tongues utter the lie that they will have the finest reward. Without a doubt, for them is the Fire, where they will be abandoned
phrases.explanation: The people attribute to Allah what they themselves dislike, yet confidently claim they will receive the best reward. The verse exposes the contradiction and warns that those who persist in falsehood will face the Fire.

phrases.translation: By Allah! We have surely sent messengers to communities before you ˹O Prophet˺, but Satan made their misdeeds appealing to them. So he is their patron today, and they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: Earlier communities also received messengers, but Satan made their wrongdoing seem attractive. Those who follow that deception have no true protector in this life and will instead face painful punishment.

phrases.translation: We have revealed to you the Book only to clarify for them what they differed about, and as a guide and mercy for those who believe
phrases.explanation: The Book is revealed to clarify matters people dispute and to serve as guidance and mercy for believers. Revelation is thus both an explanation of truth and a source of direction for those willing to follow it.

phrases.translation: And Allah sends down rain from the sky, giving life to the earth after its death. Surely in this is a sign for those who listen
phrases.explanation: Rain brings life back to dry earth, offering a visible sign of Allah’s power to renew. The verse calls it a sign for people who listen attentively to the message and reflect on what they observe.

phrases.translation: And there is certainly a lesson for you in cattle: We give you to drink of what is in their bellies, from between digested food and blood: pure milk, pleasant to drink
phrases.explanation: Milk is presented as a pure and pleasant provision produced within cattle, between what is digested and blood. The verse directs attention to a familiar source of nourishment and to the processes that make it available.

phrases.translation: And from the fruits of palm trees and grapevines you derive intoxicants as well as wholesome provision. Surely in this is a sign for those who understand
phrases.explanation: Dates and grapes can produce intoxicants as well as wholesome food. The verse invites reflection on these different outcomes, while later revelation explicitly forbids intoxicants (Quran 5:90 and 5:91), so their mention here is not an endorsement.

phrases.translation: And your Lord inspired the bees: “Make ˹your˺ homes in the mountains, the trees, and in what people construct
phrases.explanation: The bee is guided to make its home in mountains, trees, and human-built places. The verse presents this intricate behavior as inspired guidance within creation, rather than as something bees plan through human reasoning.

phrases.translation: and feed from ˹the flower of˺ any fruit ˹you please˺ and follow the ways your Lord has made easy for you.” From their bellies comes forth liquid of varying colours, in which there is healing for people. Surely in this is a sign for those who reflect
phrases.explanation: Bees feed from fruits and follow paths made easy for them, producing honey of varied colors that the verse describes as healing for people. Their behavior and useful product are signs for those who reflect.

phrases.translation: Allah has created you, and then causes you to die. And some of you are left to reach the most feeble stage of life so that they may know nothing after having known much. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, Most Capable
phrases.explanation: People pass from birth through death, and some reach old age with knowledge and abilities greatly diminished. The verse reminds readers of human dependence at every stage and affirms Allah’s complete knowledge and power.

phrases.translation: And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision. But those who have been much favoured would not share their wealth with those ˹bondspeople˺ in their possession, making them their equals. Do they then deny Allah’s favours
phrases.explanation: The verse notes differences in provision and uses people’s reluctance to make dependents equal partners in their wealth as a rhetorical comparison. It challenges denial of Allah’s favors, not as a license to mistreat anyone.

phrases.translation: And Allah has made for you spouses of your own kind, and given you through your spouses children and grandchildren. And He has granted you good, lawful provisions. Are they then faithful to falsehood and ungrateful for Allah’s favours
phrases.explanation: Spouses, children, grandchildren, and lawful provisions are named as gifts from Allah. The closing question challenges people who enjoy these blessings yet remain loyal to false gods and ungrateful to their Provider.

phrases.translation: Yet they worship besides Allah those ˹idols˺ who do not afford them any provision from the heavens and the earth, nor do they have the power to
phrases.explanation: People invoke idols that cannot provide anything from heaven or earth and lack the power to act. The sentence carries into the next verse, which draws the lesson: do not treat such beings as equals of Allah.

phrases.translation: So do not set up equals to Allah, for Allah certainly knows and you do not know
phrases.explanation: The command follows the comparison: do not assign equals to Allah, who knows the truth about what is worthy of worship while people do not. The verse cautions against projecting human assumptions onto the Creator.

phrases.translation: Allah sets forth a parable: a slave who lacks all means, compared to a ˹free˺ man to whom We granted a good provision, of which he donates ˹freely,˺ openly and secretly. Are they equal? Praise be to Allah. In fact, most of them do not know
phrases.explanation: The parable contrasts someone with no means and a person given abundant provision who gives openly and secretly. Their inequality illustrates why powerless idols cannot be treated as equal to Allah, the giver of provision.

phrases.translation: And Allah sets forth a parable of two men: one of them is dumb, incapable of anything. He is a burden on his master. Wherever he is sent, he brings no good. Can such a person be equal to the one who commands justice and is on the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: A second parable contrasts a helpless, speechless figure with someone who commands justice and follows the Straight Path. Its point is the incapacity of false gods, not a general judgment on people with speech disabilities.

phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs ˹the knowledge of˺ the unseen in the heavens and the earth. Bringing about the Hour would only take the blink of an eye, or even less. Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation: Knowledge of the unseen belongs to Allah, and bringing about the Hour is effortless for Him, like a blink or less. The verse joins the limits of human knowledge with Allah’s complete power over the end of time.

phrases.translation: And Allah brought you out of the wombs of your mothers while you knew nothing, and gave you hearing, sight, and intellect so perhaps you would be thankful
phrases.explanation: People begin life knowing nothing, then receive hearing, sight, and understanding. These capacities are gifts meant to lead to gratitude, not reasons for self-sufficiency or pride. They make learning possible.

phrases.translation: Have they not seen the birds glide in the open sky? None holds them up except Allah. Surely in this are signs for those who believe
phrases.explanation: Birds glide through open skies, sustained by the order Allah has placed in creation. Their flight is offered as a sign for believers who look beyond the scene itself to the One who sustains it.

phrases.translation: And Allah has made your homes a place to rest, and has given you tents from the hide of animals, light to handle when you travel and when you camp. And out of their wool, fur, and hair He has given you furnishings and goods for a while
phrases.explanation: Homes provide rest, while animal hides make light, portable tents for travel and camping. Wool, fur, and hair also supply furnishings and goods, showing how everyday shelter and materials are presented as temporary provisions from Allah.

phrases.translation: And Allah has provided you shade out of what He created, and has given you shelter in the mountains. He has also provided you with clothes protecting you from the heat ˹and cold˺, and armour shielding you in battle. This is how He perfects His favour upon you, so perhaps you will ˹fully˺ submit ˹to Him˺
phrases.explanation: Shade, mountain shelters, clothing, and armor protect people from exposure and attack. These everyday forms of protection are presented as favors from Allah, with the hope that recognizing them will lead people to submit gratefully to Him.

phrases.translation: But if they turn away, then your duty ˹O Prophet˺ is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly
phrases.explanation: If people reject the message, the Prophet’s responsibility is to deliver it clearly. The verse distinguishes faithful communication from control over another person’s response and leaves that response to them.

phrases.translation: They are aware of Allah’s favours, but still deny them. And most of them are ˹truly˺ ungrateful
phrases.explanation: People recognize Allah’s favors yet continue to deny them, revealing ingratitude despite awareness. The verse shows that knowing a blessing’s source does not automatically lead someone to acknowledge or obey the giver.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider, O Prophet,˺ the Day We will call ˹a prophet as˺ a witness from every faith-community. Then the disbelievers will neither be allowed to plead nor appease ˹their Lord˺
phrases.explanation: On Judgment Day, a witness will be called from every community, while those who disbelieved will have no opportunity to plead or appease their Lord. The image emphasizes a public, conclusive reckoning.

phrases.translation: And when the wrongdoers face the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺
phrases.explanation: When wrongdoers face punishment, it will neither be reduced nor postponed. The verse portrays judgment as decisive, contrasting with the respite people experience before the appointed Day, when punishment is no longer delayed.

phrases.translation: And when the polytheists see their associate-gods, they will say, “Our Lord! These are our associate-gods that we used to invoke besides You.” Their gods will throw a rebuttal at them, ˹saying,˺ “You are definitely liars.”
phrases.explanation: Those who worshipped other beings will appeal to them, but their supposed gods will call them liars. The scene shows that objects people treated as partners have neither the power nor the loyalty they imagined.

phrases.translation: They will offer ˹full˺ submission to Allah on that Day, and whatever ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them
phrases.explanation: On that Day, people submit to Allah, while the deities and claims they fabricated fail them. The verse contrasts sincere submission to the true Lord with reliance on inventions that cannot save anyone.

phrases.translation: For those who disbelieve and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, We will add more punishment to their punishment for all the corruption they spread
phrases.explanation: Those who disbelieve and obstruct others from Allah’s way face added punishment for the corruption they spread. The verse distinguishes private rejection from actively misleading and harming other people, adding accountability for damage caused beyond personal disbelief.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider, O Prophet,˺ the Day We will call against every faith-community a witness of their own. And We will call you to be a witness against these ˹people of yours˺. We have revealed to you the Book as an explanation of all things, a guide, a mercy, and good news for those who ˹fully˺ submit
phrases.explanation: A witness from each community will testify, and the Prophet will testify concerning his people. The revealed Book is described as guidance, mercy, and good news, explaining what people need for faith and right conduct.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah commands justice, grace, as well as courtesy to close relatives. He forbids indecency, wickedness, and aggression. He instructs you so perhaps you will be mindful
phrases.explanation: This verse gathers central ethical duties: justice, generous goodness, and care for relatives, while forbidding indecency, wrongdoing, and aggression. Its broad moral summary calls people to conduct that sustains dignity and social trust.

phrases.translation: Honour Allah’s covenant when you make a pledge, and do not break your oaths after confirming them, having made Allah your guarantor. Surely Allah knows all you do
phrases.explanation: People are commanded to honor pledges made in Allah’s name and not break oaths once confirmed. Invoking Allah as guarantor makes promises a serious responsibility, and Allah knows whether people keep them.

phrases.translation: Do not be like the woman who ˹foolishly˺ unravels her yarn after it is firmly spun, by taking your oaths as a means of deceiving one another in favour of a stronger group. Surely Allah tests you through this. And on the Day of Judgment He will certainly make your differences clear to you
phrases.explanation: Breaking an oath is compared to unraveling yarn after it has been firmly spun. The verse warns against abandoning a pledge to join a stronger group for advantage, reminding people that Allah will expose their choices and disputes.

phrases.translation: Had Allah willed, He could have easily made you one community ˹of believers˺, but He leaves to stray whoever He wills and guides whoever He wills. And you will certainly be questioned about what you used to do
phrases.explanation: Allah could have made everyone one believing community, but people follow different paths under His will and will answer for their actions. The verse holds divine sovereignty and human accountability together without excusing wrongdoing.

phrases.translation: And do not take your oaths as a means of deceiving one another or your feet will slip after they have been firm. Then you will taste the evil ˹consequences˺ of hindering ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, and you will suffer a tremendous punishment
phrases.explanation: Using oaths to deceive others can undo the stability people had established and hinder others from Allah’s way. The warning connects broken promises to social harm and serious consequences, not merely to a private lapse in speech.

phrases.translation: And do not trade Allah’s covenant for a fleeting gain. What is with Allah is certainly far better for you, if only you knew
phrases.explanation: A temporary worldly gain is not worth exchanging for a covenant with Allah. The verse asks people to look beyond immediate profit and trust that what Allah has in store is better and lasting.

phrases.translation: Whatever you have will end, but whatever Allah has is everlasting. And We will certainly reward the steadfast according to the best of their deeds
phrases.explanation: Everything people possess will pass away, while what belongs to Allah endures. The steadfast are promised a reward based on the best of their deeds, directing effort toward lasting rather than temporary outcomes.

phrases.translation: Whoever does good, whether male or female, and is a believer, We will surely bless them with a good life, and We will certainly reward them according to the best of their deeds
phrases.explanation: Faith and good conduct are rewarded for women and men alike with a good life and a generous reward. A good life need not mean wealth or freedom from every hardship. It is a life made good through faith and righteous action.

phrases.translation: When you recite the Quran, seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed
phrases.explanation: Before reciting the Quran, the reader is told to seek Allah’s protection from Satan. This practice acknowledges the risk of distraction and temptation and begins recitation by turning to Allah for help.

phrases.translation: He certainly has no authority over those who believe and put their trust in their Lord
phrases.explanation: Satan has no authority over those who believe and place their trust in Allah. The verse denies that he can compel them, while affirming that faith and reliance protect them from accepting his influence.

phrases.translation: His authority is only over those who take him as a patron and who—under his influence—associate ˹others˺ with Allah ˹in worship˺
phrases.explanation: Satan’s influence is over those who choose him as a patron and associate others with Allah. The verse locates responsibility in the allegiance people adopt, rather than presenting Satan as having power over everyone.

phrases.translation: When We replace a verse with another—and Allah knows best what He reveals—they say, “You ˹Muḥammad˺ are just a fabricator.” In fact, most of them do not know
phrases.explanation: The verse addresses claims that replacing one revelation with another proves fabrication. It replies that Allah knows best what He reveals, presenting any change as governed by divine knowledge rather than the Prophet’s invention.

phrases.translation: Say, “The holy spirit has brought it down from your Lord with the truth to reassure the believers, and as a guide and good news for those who submit ˹to Allah˺.”
phrases.explanation: The Holy Spirit is commonly understood here as the angel Gabriel, who brings the Quran from Allah with truth. Its purposes include reassuring believers, guiding those who submit, and bringing them good news.

phrases.translation: And We surely know that they say, “No one is teaching him except a human.” But the man they refer to speaks a foreign tongue, whereas this ˹Quran˺ is ˹in˺ eloquent Arabic
phrases.explanation: Opponents claim a human teaches Muhammad, yet point to someone whose language is foreign while the Quran is eloquent Arabic. The verse contrasts the allegation’s proposed source with the message’s language and form.

phrases.translation: Surely those who do not believe in Allah’s revelations will never be guided by Allah, and they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: Those who reject Allah’s revelations are warned that they will not receive guidance and will face painful punishment. The verse treats rejection of revelation as a serious choice with consequences, not an inconsequential disagreement.

phrases.translation: No one fabricates lies except those who disbelieve in Allah’s revelations, and it is they who are the ˹true˺ liars
phrases.explanation: The verse rejects the charge that the Prophet fabricates revelation, identifying those who deny Allah’s signs as the true liars. It turns the accusation back on people who knowingly misrepresent the message.

phrases.translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after their belief—not those who are forced while their hearts are firm in faith, but those who embrace disbelief wholeheartedly—they will be condemned by Allah and suffer a tremendous punishment
phrases.explanation: The verse distinguishes coercion from willing rejection: a person forced to speak disbelief while remaining firm in faith is excepted, while condemnation concerns those who choose disbelief wholeheartedly. It recognizes the moral difference between compulsion and conviction.

phrases.translation: This is because they prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter. Surely Allah never guides those who ˹choose to˺ disbelieve
phrases.explanation: Those who choose the immediate life of this world over the Hereafter are described as disbelievers. The verse warns against treating short-term advantage as more valuable than lasting accountability and reward.

phrases.translation: They are the ones whose hearts, ears, and eyes are sealed by Allah, and it is they who are ˹truly˺ heedless
phrases.explanation: Their hearts, ears, and eyes are described as sealed, leaving them heedless. The imagery portrays a settled refusal to take in guidance, even when signs are available to be heard, seen, and considered.

phrases.translation: Without a doubt, they will be the losers in the Hereafter
phrases.explanation: The passage states plainly that these people will be the losers in the Hereafter. Their rejection may appear advantageous for a time, but the final measure of success is what remains after worldly life.

phrases.translation: As for those who emigrated after being compelled ˹to renounce Islam˺, then struggled ˹in Allah’s cause˺, and persevered, your Lord ˹O Prophet˺ is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful after all
phrases.explanation: Those who emigrated after persecution, then struggled and remained patient, are promised Allah’s forgiveness and mercy. The verse recognizes that believers may falter or face coercion, and that sincere return and perseverance matter.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider˺ the Day ˹when˺ every soul will come pleading for itself, and each will be paid in full for what it did, and none will be wronged
phrases.explanation: On Judgment Day, every person will plead for themselves and receive full recompense for their deeds. No one will be treated unjustly, making the final accounting both personal and perfectly fair.

phrases.translation: And Allah sets forth the example of a society which was safe and at ease, receiving its provision in abundance from all directions. But its people met Allah’s favours with ingratitude, so Allah made them taste the clutches of hunger and fear for their misdeeds
phrases.explanation: A secure and prosperous community responds to abundant provision with ingratitude, then experiences hunger and fear. The example warns that comfort is a trust and that rejecting its source can bring consequences.

phrases.translation: A messenger of their own actually did come to them, but they denied him. So the torment overtook them while they persisted in wrongdoing
phrases.explanation: The community had received a messenger from among its own people, yet denied him and persisted in wrongdoing. The resulting punishment shows that familiarity with a messenger does not guarantee that a society will listen.

phrases.translation: So eat from the good, lawful things which Allah has provided for you, and be grateful for Allah’s favours, if you ˹truly˺ worship Him ˹alone˺
phrases.explanation: People are told to eat what is good and lawful, then show gratitude for Allah’s provision. True worship is connected to everyday choices, including what people consume and whether they acknowledge the source of their sustenance.

phrases.translation: He has only forbidden you ˹to eat˺ carrion, blood, swine, and what is slaughtered in the name of any other than Allah. But if someone is compelled by necessity—neither driven by desire nor exceeding immediate need—then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: The passage names carrion, blood, pork, and food dedicated to other than Allah as forbidden, while allowing what necessity requires without excess. The exception reflects mercy in hardship, not permission to indulge beyond need.

phrases.translation: Do not falsely declare with your tongues, “This is lawful, and that is unlawful,” ˹only˺ fabricating lies against Allah. Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will never succeed
phrases.explanation: People must not invent religious rules by declaring things lawful or unlawful and falsely attributing those claims to Allah. The verse makes honesty in speaking about divine commands a serious responsibility.

phrases.translation: ˹It is only˺ a brief enjoyment, then they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: The gain from such fabrication is only brief, followed by painful punishment. The verse contrasts a temporary advantage from misleading religious claims with the lasting consequences of dishonesty that they face.

phrases.translation: To the Jews, We have forbidden what We related to you before. We did not wrong them, but it was they who wronged themselves
phrases.explanation: Earlier restrictions on the Jews are recalled, while the verse clarifies that Allah did not wrong them. Their own actions brought the outcome in this history, distinguishing divine justice from arbitrary hardship.

phrases.translation: As for those who commit evil ignorantly ˹or recklessly˺, then repent afterwards and mend their ways, then your Lord is surely All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Those who do wrong through ignorance or recklessness can still repent and amend their conduct. Allah’s forgiveness and mercy remain open to them, so past wrongdoing need not prevent sincere change.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Abraham was a model of excellence: devoted to Allah, ˹perfectly˺ upright—not a polytheist—
phrases.explanation: Abraham is introduced as a model of devotion to Allah and upright faith, explicitly distinguished from polytheism. The description begins a longer account of his example, which continues in the following verse.

phrases.translation: ˹utterly˺ grateful for Allah’s favours. ˹So˺ He chose him and guided him to the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: This continues the description of Abraham: he was grateful for Allah’s blessings, so Allah chose and guided him. The verse presents gratitude as a response to favor and as a defining quality of prophetic faith.

phrases.translation: We blessed him with all goodness in this world, and in the Hereafter he will certainly be among the righteous
phrases.explanation: Abraham received goodness in this world and is promised a place among the righteous in the Hereafter. His example is not limited to worldly success, but culminates in faithfulness and lasting reward.

phrases.translation: Then We revealed to you ˹O Prophet, saying˺: “Follow the faith of Abraham, the upright, who was not one of the polytheists.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to follow Abraham’s upright faith, which rejected polytheism. The verse links Muhammad’s message to Abraham’s devotion and makes clear that true continuity lies in worshipping Allah alone.

phrases.translation: ˹Honouring˺ the Sabbath was ordained only for those who disputed about Abraham. And surely your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their disputes
phrases.explanation: The Sabbath was prescribed for those who disputed over it, and Allah will judge their disagreements on the Last Day. The verse places contested religious differences within divine judgment rather than inviting endless hostility among people.

phrases.translation: Invite ˹all˺ to the Way of your Lord with wisdom and kind advice, and only debate with them in the best manner. Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: People are to be invited to Allah’s way with wisdom and kind counsel, and disagreement should be discussed in the best manner. The verse leaves final judgment of who is guided to Allah, not to human arrogance.

phrases.translation: If you retaliate, then let it be equivalent to what you have suffered. But if you patiently endure, it is certainly best for those who are patient
phrases.explanation: Retaliation must not exceed the harm suffered, setting a limit against revenge. Yet patient endurance is described as better, distinguishing the right to seek justice from the greater virtue of restraint.

phrases.translation: Be patient ˹O Prophet˺, for your patience is only with Allah’s help. Do not grieve over those ˹who disbelieve˺, nor be distressed by their schemes
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to be patient with Allah’s help, not to grieve over those who reject the message, and not to be distressed by their schemes. The counsel redirects him toward reliance on Allah.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is with those who shun evil and who do good ˹deeds˺
phrases.explanation: Allah is with those who avoid wrongdoing and do good. This closing reassurance connects devotion with ethical action, promising divine support to people who combine awareness of Allah with kindness and righteousness.
